message.content:
Fix a bug in `apps/birdseye/internal/tui/browser.go` inside worktree `/Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/.claude/worktrees/birdseye`.

## The Bug (from bugbot)

The Browser footer renders `j/k or ↑/↓ move · q quit · esc back`, but `Browser.Update` has no Escape-key handler. There's also no "back" state — the Browser is launched as a standalone `tea.NewProgram` AFTER the picker quits (two-stage architecture). Esc does nothing; the hint misleads users.

## The Fix

Make Escape do what users actually expect (quit the browser, same as `q`) and rewrite the footer to advertise only what works.

### Edit 1: Add Escape handler

In `apps/birdseye/internal/tui/browser.go`, `Browser.Update`, find the `tea.KeyMsg` switch. The current shape:

```go
case tea.KeyMsg:
    switch msg.Type {
    case tea.KeyDown:
        b.Move(1)
        return b, nil
    case tea.KeyUp:
        b.Move(-1)
        return b, nil
    case tea.KeyRunes:
        switch string(msg.Runes) {
        case "q":
            return b, tea.Quit
        case "j":
            b.Move(1)
            return b, nil
        case "k":
            b.Move(-1)
            return b, nil
        }
    }
```

Add a `tea.KeyEsc` case alongside `tea.KeyDown` / `tea.KeyUp`:

```go
case tea.KeyEsc:
    return b, tea.Quit
```

Place it directly after `case tea.KeyUp:` and its `return b, nil`.

### Edit 2: Fix footer text

In `Browser.View()`, the footer line currently reads:

```go
footer := b.theme.Footer.Render("j/k or ↑/↓ move · q quit · esc back")
```

Replace with:

```go
footer := b.theme.Footer.Render("j/k or ↑/↓ move · q/esc quit")
```

### Edit 3: Add a regression test

Append to `apps/birdseye/internal/tui/browser_test.go`:

```go
func TestBrowserEscQuits(t *testing.T) {
	b := NewBrowser(sampleResult())
	b.SetSize(120, 30)
	_, cmd := b.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyEsc})
	if cmd == nil {
		t.Fatal("expected tea.Quit cmd from Esc")
	}
	if got, want := cmd(), tea.Quit(); got != want {
		t.Errorf("cmd msg = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestBrowserFooterReflectsActualKeybinds(t *testing.T) {
	b := NewBrowser(sampleResult())
	b.SetSize(120, 30)
	view := b.View()
	if !contains(view, "q/esc quit") {
		t.Errorf("footer should advertise q/esc quit:\n%s", view)
	}
	if contains(view, "esc back") {
		t.Errorf("footer should not advertise the removed \"esc back\":\n%s", view)
	}
}
```

The `contains` helper already exists in `browser_test.go`.

## Verify

```bash
cd /Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/.claude/worktrees/birdseye/apps/birdseye && go test -race ./internal/tui/... -v
```

All TUI tests must pass, including the two new ones.

```bash
cd /Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/.claude/worktrees/birdseye/apps/birdseye && go test -race ./... && go vet ./... && go build ./...
```

All clean.

## Commit

```bash
cd /Users/steve.briggs/projects/operations/.claude/worktrees/birdseye && git add apps/birdseye/internal/tui/browser.go apps/birdseye/internal/tui/browser_test.go && git commit -m "fix(birdseye): make Esc quit the browser and fix misleading footer"
```

## Report

- **Status:** DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT
- Summary of fixes
- Test count + race-clean
- Commit SHA
- Anything unexpected
